heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Siraya Tech ABS-GF effectively out of the box due to its factory-installed hardened steel nozzle and enclosed build chamber. You can reliably achieve print speeds up to 179 mm/s while strictly adhering to the 15 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with Bambu Liquid Glue or PVP glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 15 mm³/s in the Filament Settings to automatically throttle line speeds within the safe 179 mm/s limit.
Completely disable the Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan (0%) and keep the Chamber Fan below 30% to avoid premature shrinkage and warping.
Calibrate Pressure Advance (PA) to approximately 0.028 to 0.034 to prevent corner bulging caused by the stiffness of glass fibers.
Set Nozzle Temperature to 260°C for all layers, and set the Heated Bed to 103°C to maintain strong layer adhesion and high bed retention.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and warping from build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Cold chamber environment or drafts from the auxiliary fan inducing differential thermal contraction.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Preheat the bed at 105°C for 15 minutes to bring the enclosed chamber above 45°C, disable the auxiliary fan entirely, and use a glue stick release agent on Textured PEI.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Poor interlayer bonding and brittle Z-axis breaks
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Extruder running too cold or excessive part cooling fan blowing directly on the extrudate.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Raise nozzle printing temperature to 265°C, reduce Part Cooling Fan to a 0% minimum and 15% maximum, and ensure volumetric flow does not exceed 15 mm³/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Filament snapping or feeding errors in the PTFE pathway
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption combined with glass-fiber rigidity causing brittleness along the tight bends of the feed tubes.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated dryer at 80°C for 6 to 8 hours before use, and run the spool directly from an external roller or drybox to reduce bending strain.

faq.question: Can I feed Siraya Tech ABS-GF through the Bambu Lab AMS?
faq.answer: While it can feed through the AMS, the abrasive glass fibers will rapidly wear the stock plastic feeder funnels and internal PTFE lines; running directly from an external spool holder or drybox is recommended for high-volume use.

faq.question: Does Siraya Tech ABS-GF require drying before printing on the X1C?
faq.answer: Yes, ABS is hygroscopic and moisture exacerbates brittleness and voids in fiber-filled polymers; dry at 75°C to 80°C for at least 6 hours prior to printing.

faq.question: Will Siraya Tech ABS-GF wear out the Bambu X1C stock nozzle?
faq.answer: No, the Bambu Lab X1C comes standard with a hardened steel nozzle and hardened steel extruder gears, making it fully rated for abrasive glass-fiber filaments.

faq.question: Should I keep the front glass door and top lid closed when printing this filament?
faq.answer: Yes, keep the X1C completely closed to retain ambient chamber heat and prevent drafts, which are critical to preventing ABS-GF from warping or delaminating.
